answer: Restricting to what the data actually support: there is no unconditional Black completion advantage — Black BA completion is below White in every pooled SES quartile (Q1 0.44% vs 1.78%, Q2 1.33% vs 4.32%, Q3 1.63% vs 3.73%, Q4 3.03% vs 3.67%). The only data-grounded form of a Black "advantage" is conditional and interactive: Black completion rises substantially faster with SES than White's (univariable logistic BLACK×SES = +0.76, 95% CI 0.26–1.26, p≈0.003; p≈0.006 after adjusting for sex, ASVAB and class percentile), so the Black−White completion gap is widest (most negative, ≈ −2.1 to −2.2 pp) at low-to-middle SES, narrows monotonically as SES rises, crosses parity around SES ≈ +1.0 to +1.3 on the externally normed SES scale, and turns mildly positive (Black above White) in the upper SES tail. The advantage in completion rates for Black students is therefore most pronounced at UPPER-middle-to-HIGH socioeconomic levels (roughly the upper quartile, SES > ≈ +0.5, with crossover near +1.0–1.3 and the largest predicted gaps in the extreme upper tail), not at low SES. This high-SES conclusion is suggestive rather than definitive: it rests on sparse Black samples in the upper tail (35 Black at SES ≥ +1.5 with 3 completions; 8 BA events among 232 Black at SES > +0.5), and the 95% CI on the predicted Black−White gap includes parity across the entire SES range — it excludes zero only below SES ≈ +0.7, where Black are significantly below White.

payload.hypothesis: Black students show no unconditional completion advantage (Black below White in every SES quartile); the only data-supported Black advantage is conditional and interactive — Black BA-completion rises significantly faster with SES than White's (logistic BLACK x SES = +0.76, p~0.003), so the Black-White gap narrows monotonically with SES, crosses parity near SES ~ +1.0 to +1.3 (externally normed scale) and turns positive in the upper tail. The advantage is therefore most pronounced at upper-middle-to-high socioeconomic levels (~upper quartile, SES > +0.5; crossover +1.0-1.3), not at low SES, though the high-SES estimate is imprecise (small Black cells: 35 Black at SES>=1.5, 3 completions; CI includes parity across the whole SES range, excluding 0 only below SES~+0.7 where Black are significantly below White).
payload.workflow: 1) Load 8,773-row NLS SES file; drop stray index column; BA as binary. 2) Pooled-quartile strata: completion rate by race, percentage-point gaps Black minus White and Black minus all-others with Wald CIs (outputs/quartile_strata.csv). 3) Sensitivity: tertiles and fixed reference thresholds low<−0.5/mid/high>+0.5 (CSVs). 4) Univariable logistic BA ~ SES + race + SES×race (White ref); primary interaction test = BLACK×SES (coef +0.76, p=0.0028). 5) Headline deliverable: continuous-SES predicted Black−White pp-gap curve with delta-method 95% CI band (outputs/predicted_gap_curve.csv + .svg); crossover SES≈1.26; CI excludes 0 only below SES≈0.70. 6) Robustness: adjusted logistic adding sex, ASVAB z, percentile z (BLACK×SES +0.76, p=0.0057; crossover≈0).
